items.ig_caption:
The breach investigators got breached. 🕵️

What Chainalysis disclosed (30 Oct):
→ An external actor got into its systems and internal tools using what it calls "offensive agentic techniques"
→ Accessed: user IDs, full names, email addresses and organisation role labels, which it calls "non-sensitive"
→ No evidence so far of access to investigation data (graphs, notes, cases), clear-text passwords, MFA secrets or session tokens
→ It hasn't said how many customers are affected, named an AI model, or said how much a human directed the attack
→ Chainalysis says it is unrelated to the Binance theft

Why it matters: names + work emails + job roles of crypto investigators is exactly what a targeted phishing campaign needs. Warn users about unexpected password resets and login prompts, and make sure 2FA is on.

cover.hook: Files renamed .L0CK3D. Synology NAS boxes hit by ransomware.
cover.sub: Security firm 360 warns C3RB3R ransomware is encrypting Synology NAS devices through DSM flaws. Synology's fix: update DSM.

slides.title: What's happening
slides.body: 360 says C3RB3R, a Cerber variant, has been hitting Synology NAS devices since early October. Encrypted files get a .L0CK3D extension and a read-me3.txt ransom note pointing to a Tor site.

slides.title: Which flaws
slides.body: Synology says attackers are exploiting a flaw it fixed in December 2024 on devices running outdated DSM. Reports citing 360 also link CVE-2026-13639 and CVE-2026-13684, fixed on 18 Sep.

slides.label: CVSS · CVE-2026-13639 & CVE-2026-13684: unauthenticated remote file read/write
slides.note: Synology-SA-26:13 lists no workaround: upgrade only

slides.title: Fixed DSM versions
slides.body: DSM 7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 or 7.2.1-69057-12, or later. Older, unsupported DSM releases are the ones Synology says are being targeted.

slides.title: What to do
items: Update DSM to a fixed release today
Remove port forwarding; use a VPN for remote access
Disable the default admin account, turn on 2FA
Keep locked snapshots plus an offline backup

items.ig_caption:
Files renamed .L0CK3D. A ransom note in every folder. On a NAS. 🔒

What we know (IT-Connect, 29 Oct; Synology advisory):
→ Chinese security firm 360 says C3RB3R, a Cerber variant, has been encrypting Synology NAS devices since early October
→ Synology warns attackers are exploiting a flaw it fixed in December 2024 on devices running outdated DSM
→ Reports citing 360 also link CVE-2026-13639 and CVE-2026-13684: both CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated remote file read/write, fixed on 18 Sep (Synology-SA-26:13)
→ Synology lists no workaround: updating is the fix

What to do this week: update DSM (7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 or 7.2.1-69057-12 or later), remove direct port forwarding and use a VPN, disable the default admin account, turn on 2FA, and keep locked snapshots plus an offline backup. RAID is not a backup.

items.x_text:
n0n ransomware: SOCRadar found the operator's exposed server. AI spend topped $7,216, with an OpenCode agent wired to 154 model entries. Yet every documented break-in used weak or stolen credentials (RDP, FortiGate SSL-VPN stuffing).

#Ransomware #AISecurity
items.ig_caption:
$7,216 spent on AI. Then the server was left open for anyone to see. 🤖

What SOCRadar found (via The Register, 30 Oct):
→ The n0n ransomware operator, a newcomer since September with 108 claimed victims, left a public file server holding 1,719 files: scripts, ransomware source code and an AI coding agent setup
→ AI costs passed $7,216 by 22 Oct, using OpenCode with 154 model entries across seven providers, some marketed as "uncensored"
→ The AI wrote and debugged hundreds of scripts; SOCRadar found no evidence of a fully autonomous attack
→ The way in was boring: every documented compromise relied on weak or stolen credentials, via RDP scanning, FortiGate SSL-VPN credential stuffing and exposed cloud keys
→ The operator deleted backups in some cases

Why it matters: AI made this crew faster, not smarter. Phishing-resistant MFA on VPN and RDP, rotated cloud keys and backups that can't be deleted would have blocked most of it.

items.send_to: whoever approves dev tools at work

cover.hook: Your AI coding assistant has a browser. Researchers broke 5 of them.
cover.sub: Forever Security's EMBRACE research: Cursor, Copilot, Codex, VS Code and Claude Desktop. Codex and VS Code unpatched at publication.

slides.title: What they found
slides.body: Flaws in the embedded browsers of five desktop AI assistants: code execution on the host in Cursor, a spoofed address bar in GitHub Copilot, and local files reading outside the project in Claude Desktop, Codex and VS Code.

slides.title: What was reachable
slides.body: Per the researchers, the file-read issue could reach SSH keys, .env files, package manager tokens, cloud credentials, browser session data and private source code.

slides.title: The user step
slides.body: Cursor needed one approval of an agent's command. The file-read issue needed the user to open a malicious local file, but the link came from the assistant itself, so the click felt routine.

slides.title: Patch status (29 Oct)
slides.body: Cursor patched 1 Oct. Copilot fixed in 1.1.29 on 13 Oct. Anthropic accepted the Claude Desktop report. OpenAI hadn't responded and Microsoft declined it: Codex and VS Code unpatched at publication.

slides.title: What to do
items: Inventory AI assistants on developer laptops
Update Cursor and Copilot to fixed builds
Don't open untrusted links or files in built-in browsers
Keep SSH keys and cloud creds out of plain files

items.question: Do you know which AI assistants are installed on your developers' laptops?
items.x_text:
EMBRACE: Forever Security broke the embedded browsers in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Codex, VS Code and Claude Desktop: host code execution, address-bar spoofing, local file reads. Codex and VS Code were unpatched at publication.

#AISecurity #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
Your AI coding assistant ships with a browser. Researchers broke five of them. 🧑‍💻

What Forever Security found (EMBRACE research, 29 Oct):
→ Cursor: a web page could get code to run on the host after one approval of an agent's command
→ GitHub Copilot: a page could spoof the address bar, showing a different site than the one loaded
→ Claude Desktop, Codex and VS Code: a malicious local file could read files outside the project, including SSH keys, .env files, cloud credentials and source code
→ Cursor patched on 1 Oct; Copilot fixed in 1.1.29 on 13 Oct; Anthropic accepted the report
→ OpenAI hadn't responded and Microsoft declined the report: Codex and VS Code were unpatched at publication

Why it matters: the built-in browser loads untrusted pages, is driven by an agent, and sits next to your developers' keys. Inventory the AI assistants on dev machines, update Cursor and Copilot, and treat links and files the assistant opens as untrusted.

Apple threat notifications: a new wave of mercenary spyware alerts went to targeted iPhone users in 99 countries, per CyberScoop. Over 150 countries notified to date. Apple advises Lockdown Mode. No alert doesn't rule out infection.

#Spyware #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
99 countries. One new wave of Apple spyware warnings. 📱

What happened (via CyberScoop, 30 Oct):
→ Apple sent new threat notifications about mercenary spyware to targeted users in 99 countries
→ Apple says it has now notified users in over 150 countries in total; the previous big batch went out in August
→ Recipients include journalists and documentary filmmakers. Apple doesn't attribute the attacks to anyone
→ Myth: no alert means no spyware. Citizen Lab's John Scott-Railton says a lack of notification does not rule out an infection

What to do: a real Apple alert never asks you to click links, open files or install anything; check it by signing in at account.apple.com. If you're at risk, turn on Lockdown Mode, keep devices updated, and contact Access Now's Digital Security Helpline. Be wary of paid "spyware removal" services.
